biophysical_burden.boundary: Accumulated satellite-observed inundation across catalogued large events; overlapping event footprints are not interpreted as unique land area.

human_economic_burden.boundary: Source-estimated people directly affected by observed events, not the modeled population living in probability zones.

extent.geographic_scope: Global large-event observation and 188-country current flood-probability-zone exposure
extent.quality_control_boundary: The satellite catalogue excludes smaller events, events without suitable MODIS imagery and events failing quality control; clouds, vegetation, permanent water, event timing and population grids affect estimates. The probability-zone assessment depends on the Fathom hazard model, 2020 population, poverty surveys, protection assumptions and a >0.15 m inundation threshold. Neither study supplies a global asset-value total.

source_snapshot.source_separation_rule: Only the satellite-observed inundation area, affected-population range and 18-year observation period enter the impact composite. Probability-zone population and poverty estimates corroborate present exposure and contract fit but do not add points.
excluded_from_scoring: events absent from the quality-controlled catalogue

transformations.formula: Normalize the source-reported 2.23 million km2 accumulated inundation across 913 quality-controlled large events; do not deduplicate or reinterpret it as current floodplain area.
Use the midpoint of the source-reported 255-290 million affected-population range while retaining both bounds.
Normalize the 2000-2018 observation span once; no annual trend or projection is inferred.
Use global scope while retaining the event-selection and quality-control omissions; missing floods never become zero.

receipts.uncertainty: The satellite catalogue excludes smaller events, events without suitable MODIS imagery and events failing quality control; clouds, vegetation, permanent water, event timing and population grids affect estimates. The probability-zone assessment depends on the Fathom hazard model, 2020 population, poverty surveys, protection assumptions and a >0.15 m inundation threshold. Neither study supplies a global asset-value total.
receipts.freshness: Satellite event observations through 2018; 2020 population exposure assessment published 2022; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T19:08:17.478Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: The global satellite study quantifies accumulated inundation area, directly affected population, an 18-year observation window and global event extent. The 188-country assessment independently confirms that the metric is population inside a declared flood-probability and depth zone.
higher_priority_failures: The operational Aqueduct snapshot serves baseline water stress, not flood-zone exposure.

The observational event record ends in 2018 and is not a current 20-year annual or 60-month global panel; the 2020 probability-zone exposure is modeled and is retained as context rather than silently scored as current observation.
